title: Wearing the Agent: From Group Chats to Glasses — Sai Krishna Rallabandi
talk_summary: A talk about deploying a personal agent (Judith) in group-chat and wearable settings, focused on three problems: security at the action surface, memory curation, and privacy-aware routing of information to the right people. It is mostly conceptual with a few concrete mechanisms (deterministic action-boundary guards, atomic-fact memory extraction, per-user LoRA adapters for permissions).

takeaways.technique: Guard at the action surface, not the input
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of filtering everything the agent reads (which gates all input and adds latency), they let the agent read broadly and place a deterministic guard (regex/traditional NLP, optionally a small fine-tuned model) at the moment of action — reading env vars, exporting data, touching secrets/configs — and classify into allow / needs-approval / block.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of guarding whatever the agent reads, we let the agent read everything and then design a guard which is deterministic.
takeaways.numbers: Naive approach ~50% on Inspect-Agent benchmark (coin flip), improved with learned model; ~90% of attacks observed to involve skill collisions.

takeaways.technique: Separate data channel from instruction channel
takeaways.what_they_do: A LoRA-fine-tuned small model classifies fetched content (web pages, messages, issues) as benign/malignant and strips injected instructions so the agent performs only the intended task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: separate the data channel firstly from the instruction channel and only give out that information which is purely benign

takeaways.technique: Atomic-fact extraction instead of transcript compaction
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than storing full conversations and compacting when they overflow, extract atomic high-value facts, score them for relevance/hierarchy/temporality, and retrieve via a graph rather than crawling everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A probably smarter way would be to ex extract some form of atomic information, atomic bits from this conversation.

takeaways.what_they_do: Train a simple model/SLM that continually scores what to keep vs forget as context evolves, enabling knowledge-based compaction rather than blind truncation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they learn a relevance scorer which keeps scoring continually

takeaways.what_they_do: A small classifier (even logistic regression) decides whether the agent should respond at all and to whom, to counter agents being over-proactive and over-articulate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they tend to o be over proact be over uh articulative when they are not asked questions

takeaways.technique: Per-user LoRA adapters to bake in permissions
takeaways.what_they_do: Share one memory layer but train separate LoRA adapters per user so access permissions are enforced by the model rather than by code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: train different uh Laura adapters on top of of each adapter for each of the users. Therefore the permissions are baked in.
